correctness.rationale: For a deck with n fixed types each of multiplicity m, the pathwise identity T-m=count of correct predictions at multi-maximal ties follows by telescoping the maximum remaining count. The exact score compensator is S=sum_k W_k/(nm-k). Centered hypergeometric counts have the n-bridge martingale FCLT; on intervals away from endpoints, bounded jumps and quadratic variation give joint convergence with the noise. Martingale-integrand convergence for argmax requires smoothing: Gaussian pairwise near-tie occupation tends to zero and Itô-isometry bounds control the approximation. Endpoint hypergeometric sqrt(1-u) estimates control the compensator tail; qv controls the martingale tail. Brownian rank Tanaka yields 1/2 symmetric local time of the top two coordinate gap; n=2 yields the Rayleigh law. Direct independent finite-deck enumeration verified exact pathwise score-tie identity and compensator equality for five small n,m, but does not prove weak convergence. A specialist proof check of selector smoothing remains a stated risk.

Identifying its fixed-type non-Gaussian distributional limit by top-rank collision local time answers a concrete statistical probability question, with an exact known two-type normalization.
